action_needed: Dédalo now runs on Bun 1.4.3, which fixes a runtime defect that could leave a process waiting forever, at full CPU, on a program it had started.
Every AI request now counts against daily limits set per user and per profile, and generated answers need their own permission.
The browser installer is gone — install with the terminal installer; a server with no configuration now refuses to start.
SELinux lets the web server reach the Dédalo engine only, and no backup or rollback step runs as root on files the service user can change.
The terminal installer sets up the whole host: production, Docker and trial install in one run.
The site builder's OpenCode driver loads only the configuration the site builder states.
A site builder agent turn can no longer leave configuration in its home directory for the next turn to read.
Thesauri are offered from one exported manifest, hierarchy.json, and nothing but declared dependencies is pre-selected.
The PostgreSQL socket you give the installer is now the one the server connects through (`DB_SOCKET`).
Docker installations now pull a published, signed Dédalo image, or build it locally if you prefer, and record the choice in `.dedalo.env`.
Installations now choose their domain ontologies (Oral history by default) and install what each one declares it depends on; the install database carries only the core ontologies and no test data.
"The Publication API v1 on a publication host answers again: its configuration names the release that runs."
New installations are connected to the official update server and always have the Languages thesaurus; a server restarted by systemd or Docker must now declare `DEDALO_SUPERVISED=true`.

"A publication host can now be installed with one guided command, `provision init`, on Debian, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, and RHEL, Rocky or Alma 9 and 10 with SELinux; the Publication API v1 runs in a FastCGI pool of its own."
The publication host provisioner now refuses an instance declaration that anyone other than root could change.
Publication host provisioning works with Apache on Debian and Ubuntu.
Several publication hosts on one server are checked for isolation.
The site builder's Claude Code agent no longer loads configuration from the site's own files, and refuses a Claude Code that cannot be told not to.
The site builder's agent can no longer choose its own agent program, read another site's activity, or stall a turn with a planted brief.
A site's AI turn no longer runs commands planted in the site's git settings, and the site builder says why it refuses a run.
The site builder runs each site's AI agent as that site's own system user, from units that root installs. systemd 248 is now enough, and `provision apply` must run before the updated daemon starts.
Only profiles granted the assistant tool can use the assistant.
The site builder can no longer start its agent units through polkit
Outbound fetches now refuse every IPv6 route to an internal address.

entries.title: Logging back in as another user no longer saves the previous user's pending edit.
Rich text is cleaned by a real HTML parser when it is saved.
Searching or sorting by a field the user may not see no longer reveals its values.
A search whose conditions are joined by OR at the top level no longer returns records outside the user's projects.
Activity and Time-machine sections no longer offer a section toolbar
Checkboxes and radio buttons inside a tool now wear the tool's colour, not Dédalo orange
The user activity chart names actions in your language.
Searching a thesaurus branch with all its descendants costs the same however large the branch.
The site builder now says why it refused, and which refusals clear by themselves.
A failed agent turn in the site builder now says what went wrong, in your language.
The tools of a section list are now grouped in one Tools menu.
The audio/video viewer window now fits the media: no size jump on play, no black bars.
A slow server shows one quiet progress bar instead of a pile of warning bubbles.
A tool that opens in a dialog appears at once, even on a slow connection.
The password field shows its requirements and says clearly whether a password was saved.
Tools no longer show a “Developed by” footer; *Update cache* uses the standard tool action button.
The history of a field that links records is one timeline, whatever the working language.
Tools work on phones
Tool windows and dialogs: readable buttons and one consistent header
The search pane on a phone: tap a field to add it, no drag needed
The search group operator (AND / OR) now shows a "Search operator" tooltip on hover.
A new tool imports journal articles from any OAI-PMH/OJS source directly into Publication records.
A new tool imports coin-auction lots (jesusvico.com, biddr.com, aureo.com, numisbids.com, sixbid.com) directly into Numismatic Data records.
The RDF import fills the record again, and links or creates its related records.
The CSV import can now add a column's values to what a record already holds, instead of replacing them.
The date picker button works in the search panel on a phone
The date picker opens again on a phone (edit and search).
The projects picker follows a user's project assignments at once.

No change can place a thesaurus term below itself any more — not two tree moves made at the same moment, nor an edit, import or restore — and two people changing a term's broader terms at the same time no longer erase each other's change.
The PDF extractor shows extracted text exactly as the PDF holds it, and its HTML mode is cleaned on the server.
Moving, adding and reordering terms in the thesaurus tree is recorded in each term's history and updates its "modified by" and "modified date".
The Time Machine history of a Hierarchies record opens again instead of failing with an internal error.
Thesaurus: adding a child to a term now shows its expand arrow at once.
The error page shows its Raspa background again.
Confirm-dialog buttons keep the space between icon and label on a phone.
The CSV import's column mapper shows a real value from the file as each column's *Sample data*, not the column's own name.
The CSV importer recognises the common record columns again (created and modified by/date, and the rest of the record information).
The pinned-records chip of a section list tells where the pins come from and disappears when they are cleared.
The "Show buttons" label no longer covers the search buttons on a phone.
The MARC21 and Zotero imports refuse a computed field, and an AI agent can remove one child of a thesaurus term.
Error messages now show their details instead of placeholders like `{section_tipo}`.
Adding or removing a term's children from its Children field now saves.
A language field whose stored language is no longer a project language shows it again.
The subtitles tool opens again instead of failing with an error.
Browsers that ran Dédalo v6 no longer load stale v6 scripts after the upgrade to v7.
Autocomplete searches work again in pickers with a related-record field, and the field inputs search as you type
Result lists spanning several sections show every row again
RDF import now works with linked-data servers that redirect, and respects their robots.txt.
Small editing forms no longer show tool buttons they turn off.
A duplicated record never points at the original record's image or document files.
Export — a marker shows where a dragged column will land.
Export preset editor — the name field no longer offers a second value.
Export presets panel — one-line rows, lighter design, click a row to apply.
Dialogs with an edit form leave room for the field's button bar.
A tall dialog title no longer covers the dialog's content.
The Ontology parser button in the Ontology area is readable again
Restoring or undeleting a record now updates every list and search that shows who references it.
Tool action buttons show a spinning ring while working, not a solid disc.
The Update cache tool scrolls to its result
Reverting the same bulk run a second time no longer reports records as "not reverted" when nothing changed.
Removing a dataframe frame no longer deletes the frame's target record.
Choosing an option in a radio-button field no longer makes the field flicker.
Applying a Time Machine value no longer breaks a record's rated portal.
Searches through a related section now answer negations and combined conditions correctly.
The time machine shows a field's frames and their values as they were at the chosen change.
A section that fails to load says why, and can be reloaded
Deleting a record's data now also empties every dataframe of its fields.
A field's history now keeps its dataframe with it, and restoring an entry restores both.
A field's history now shows the dataframe it had at that moment.
A transliteration saved in its language no longer replaces the base form.
Reverting a batch run now restores exactly what the run replaced, and says what it could not.
A CSV import that carries the modification date and user keeps them on records whose cells embed dataframe frames.
Searching through a related record (e.g. a coin's type → its mint → the mint's name) is much faster.
Saving a language selector is instant again and keeps showing only the project languages.
Every AI request now counts against daily limits set per user and per profile, and generated answers need their own permission.
SELinux lets the web server reach the Dédalo engine only, and no backup or rollback step runs as root on files the service user can change.
The site builder's OpenCode driver loads only the configuration the site builder states.
A site builder agent turn can no longer leave configuration in its home directory for the next turn to read.
Root's writes under a directory another account controls now land only in the exact directory expected.
The publication host provisioner now refuses an instance declaration that anyone other than root could change.
Master media folders are protected whatever their letter case
Uploaded script files under the media folder answer "not found" on Apache
Working files under the media folder are never served, on Apache or nginx
The assistant no longer proposes changes its own apply step would refuse.
Removing a linked record from a portal now checks the portal field and the record's projects.
Asking a vision model for proposals, or identifying a photograph with an external encoder, now requires the identification tool permission.
Searches through a related field only reach the sections that field links to, and that the user may read
The site builder's Claude Code agent no longer loads configuration from the site's own files, and refuses a Claude Code that cannot be told not to.
The site builder's agent can no longer choose its own agent program, read another site's activity, or stall a turn with a planted brief.
A site's AI turn no longer runs commands planted in the site's git settings, and the site builder says why it refuses a run.
The site builder runs each site's AI agent as that site's own system user, from units that root installs. systemd 248 is now enough, and `provision apply` must run before the updated daemon starts.
The thesaurus term picker grants link mode only from a profile, never from a blanket rule.
Translation, imports, cache rebuilds, uploads and bulk reverts now check permissions on every record and field they write.
The assistant can no longer search or count records of a section the user may not read.
Only profiles granted the assistant tool can use the assistant.
Translation, transcription and RDF-import fetches now connect to the address the SSRF guard vetted (DNS rebinding closed); network failures report a typed reason.
Posterframes, audio streams and clip downloads now respect the component's own permission and the user's projects.
Ontology identifiers are checked on every read and write, and the database now refuses malformed ones.
Stored password hashes are no longer sent to the browser.

Site builder agent turns and builds run in a private network namespace and reach the outside only by hostname, through the daemon's egress gate; the Publication API key no longer reaches the agent, and AGENT_EGRESS_ALLOW is refused.
The site builder can no longer start its agent units through polkit
Transcription actions check the audiovisual component and the user's projects before they touch a recording.
Every write through a tool, the assistant or the record doors now asks the same four questions, in the same order.
Outbound fetches now refuse every IPv6 route to an internal address.
The browser installer is gone — install with the terminal installer; a server with no configuration now refuses to start.
The debug info bar is one thin line on a tablet or phone
The diffusion publication ledger drops the indexes it never used.
A publication job now says when it has moved on to the linked records.
Large exports no longer load the whole selection into the server's memory.
Thesauri are offered from one exported manifest, hierarchy.json, and nothing but declared dependencies is pre-selected.
Ontology dependencies are declared in the master's *Dependencies* field, say whether an ontology or a thesaurus is needed, and can be optional.
Installations now choose their domain ontologies (Oral history by default) and install what each one declares it depends on; the install database carries only the core ontologies and no test data.

"On a publication host with fapolicyd, the trust of the agent, its Bun and every Publication API release it installs is now kept by the host itself: no trust lines to run by hand, and a rollback is trusted too."
"On RHEL, Rocky and Alma, the v2 API of a site installed in its home now uses the publication host's own SELinux type, as in the system layout."
The guided publication-host install now proposes the v1 database connection it finds on the host.
"`install.sh` now asks you to trust its Bun in the instance's own fapolicyd file, and says when to remove it."
The publication host's guided install is now proven on Ubuntu 26.04, including the agent's one root permission under its new sudo.
A publication host on its own machine is now proven on Ubuntu 26.04, from the panel's kit to the first publication.
New installations are connected to the official update server and always have the Languages thesaurus; a server restarted by systemd or Docker must now declare `DEDALO_SUPERVISED=true`.
"`provision check` now refuses a publication host where a service could not read or run its own code, and an `engine_group` that is one of the instance's own groups."
The Ontology area can now be opened by global administrators whose profile grants it, not only by root.
Preparing the publication host agent now installs exactly the locked dependency versions, and only the ones it runs with.
"`provision check` no longer reads as an error when it lists the changes to make."
The in-browser AI runtime is updated to transformers.js 4.3.0, running on the exact ONNX Runtime build it was made for.
The code-update panel now leads with its verdict and the update button; the reference facts fold away.
The maintenance *Unit test area* only offers the JS test runner and the test-table reset where they can work.
Hitting a database limit now shows a clear "try again" error, and maintenance runs on its own database connections.
The official update server for v7 installations is v7.master.dedalo.dev.
A published code release is now built from a release tag (`vX.Y.Z`); developer builds come from `master`.
Building and serving code releases now has its own maintenance panel, Serve Code.
Serving your ontology to other installations now has its own maintenance panel, Serve Ontology.
The diffusion job queue shows who started each publication.
The publication job queue shows how long each finished job took.
The publication server panel shows an estimated time remaining for the running jobs.
The publication tool names the target database of an SQL publication.
A Production instance can be installed by hand again, step by step, exactly as the installer does it.
A production install can live in any folder and run as an existing account.
The terminal installer sets up the whole host: production, Docker and trial install in one run.
The installer asks its questions in the terminal, checks each answer as you give it, and shows the whole plan before it installs anything.
The terminal installer draws full-screen at a capable terminal, and can abort an interrupted install
The command-line installer checks every answer before it writes anything, and an interrupted install can be resumed.
Docker installations now pull a published, signed Dédalo image, or build it locally if you prefer, and record the choice in `.dedalo.env`.
A publication host on another machine installs from one kit file built on the work host.
After an install from a kit converges, `provision init` offers to remove the kit file it was given.
Two-machine publication hosts pair from one sealed, passphrase-protected file.
"`provision init` reports the sealed pairing package as stale once the work host has used it, and removes it on request."
A new publication host can be drafted, kitted and paired from the Publication hosts panel.
A publication host whose declaration drops the Publication API v1 now has its v1 pool, log rotation and v1 files removed by `provision apply`.
A publication host can now serve the Publication API v2 only, without the Publication API v1.
On Docker installations, the Update code panel now shows how to install each release, and can hand the update to an optional host updater.
The Update code panel shows each release's notes before you install it.
The backup panel now says when backups are manual.
On an nginx publication host, the media map is now pushed by Apply media rules, and shared safely by every instance on the host.

"A publication host can now be installed with one guided command, `provision init`, on Debian, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, and RHEL, Rocky or Alma 9 and 10 with SELinux; the Publication API v1 runs in a FastCGI pool of its own."
The Publication hosts panel now shows in red a publication server whose Bun differs from the version the work system pins.
Several publication hosts on one server are checked for isolation.
A paired publication server now gets the Publication APIs matching the work system's version, can keep a verified copy of the published media, and is checked from the public side.
The publication hosts panel shows each copy-mode host's media copy, and root can bring one host back in sync on demand.
A separate publication server can now run a small agent that the work system pairs with, to install the Publication APIs, apply media rules and report status, without root access.
A separate publication server can now serve published media from shared storage, with its own access rules.
The maintenance panel now shows each paired publication server, and can apply its media rules or roll back a Publication API release.
The Docker and Trial installers check, before you type `yes`, that the official image of your version is published — a beta has none, so choose Build.
Dédalo now runs on Bun 1.4.3, which fixes a runtime defect that could leave a process waiting forever, at full CPU, on a program it had started.
Publication progress no longer runs past its estimate while a job is still working.
The installer refuses an installed instance's name up front, and a refused Review checks again on install.
The installer's System check edit, Review re-check and default-site note, salt hint and Docker abort messages now match what happens.
The installer names a killed engine and shows what the engine said while it stopped.
Installer: one interruption block on Ctrl-C, a resume that re-checks and tells everything, the salt on a terminal resume, and clearer screens.
"Production and by-hand installs: one backup directory from the first run, another web server refused, and an abort that tells a started instance from one that never started."
An install interrupted during the database restore can be resumed or undone at once, and the host shows the engine's own refusal.
Docker and trial installs: the local image build reports the release version, nginx always publishes its ports, and a resume re-checks the site.
Every installer front end ends with the same *To do on this host* list, the salt's read command in it.
Docker and Trial installs probe the media gate again on resume, and name their images and locks correctly.
The full-screen installer's closing lines start on a clean line, and the manual removal list covers Bun and a gpasswd after an abort.
Installer re-checks, interrupts and messages say things once and at the right moment.
A Production install interrupted before its server ever ran is removed whole by --abort, and the production pages match what the installer does.
The installer says what its system check would refuse on the Review, before `yes`, and a refusal never loses your answers.
A Docker installation that builds its image here now updates from a clean snapshot of the release, like the install
The official Dédalo image carries Dédalo's own url, description and licence labels.
On the Docker and trial routes, `--abort` removes an install interrupted before the engine container ever started, database included.
The publication tool shows every publication of a section, including two that share a database definition.
An interrupted or stopped install now resumes, an abort says exactly what it undid, and an instance that never served can be removed completely.
The Docker and Trial installs now start a working nginx, publish only what they serve, and say why a check failed.
The Production install now completes on RHEL 10 with SELinux, says before the install what you must do yourself, and keeps an unknown address away from every instance.
A tch install no longer asks for crm, a local image build reports its real version, and a production instance keeps its backups in one place.
The installer's screens now say what each route does, take a typed `yes` everywhere, and write `--write-answers` at the Review.
The installer's System check no longer fails on a host without PostgreSQL
The installer no longer leaves Bun's cache in an existing hosting account's home.
The update-ontology warning no longer claims your local ontology will be deleted.
The PostgreSQL socket you give the installer is now the one the server connects through (`DB_SOCKET`).
On Docker, the browser client now always matches the engine that is running.
The installation guides now install the watchdog and rollback scripts, tell existing servers how to declare supervision, and give RHEL a complete systemd unit.
The install database is compiled from the repository and proven by a fresh install before it ships.
"**Probe media** on a new copy-mode publication host no longer reports a problem before anything is published."
"The guided publication-host install now runs on RHEL 9 with SELinux enforcing and fapolicyd: the polkit rules directory, the SELinux tools and fapolicyd's trust are judged as EL ships them."
"On RHEL, Rocky and Alma with SELinux, the Publication API v2 of a site installed in its home now starts: systemd may read its settings and its release links."
"The guided install of a publication host now gives a working command for the newer AppStream runtime of the v1 API on RHEL, Rocky and Alma 10."
"On a publication host with fapolicyd's `allow_filesystem_mark = 1`, the agent keeps its right to reload the web server and start its services."
On an nginx publication host, a media map that stops nginx at its reload is now rolled back and nginx restarted, and the panel counts a map that is not loaded as a red check.
The publication host's guided install now configures the running web server when both Apache and nginx are installed.
"When `provision apply` is refused and you answer `manual`, the guided install no longer goes on with the steps that need it."
"The guided install no longer refuses when you keep the default answer of an optional question."
"Pairing from the sealed package: the guide puts the copy where the Dédalo user can read it, and an unreadable copy says why."
"On RHEL, Rocky and Alma, a publication host in the system layout now starts its v2 API: the provisioner installs its own small SELinux policy module."
"Rotating a publication host's token now restarts its agent."
"Upgrading a publication host's agent from a new kit no longer leaves the agent stopped on a host with fapolicyd."
"The Publication API v1 on a publication host answers again: its configuration names the release that runs."
The Publication API v1 error log on a publication host is now rotated.
"Publication API v1 releases install on a publication host with fapolicyd's `allow_filesystem_mark = 1`."
Container installs take their nightly backups again, and the full-stack install no longer stops at "directories".
"`./install.sh` runs on macOS again (and wherever Docker's storage lives in a VM)."
"The publication-host pairing command now names a command you can run, and says why it cannot read a copied file."
The auction-URL and journal-URL import tools now declare the sections they belong to.
Ontologies re-installed by an ontology update keep their typology and name instead of moving to "Others".
A tool whose code fails to load no longer appears in every section.
Code updates no longer refuse over a file an older release shipped and a newer one removed.
Publishing no longer fails creating a MariaDB integer column sized by `varchar`.
A publication table too wide for MariaDB is refused by name before publishing starts.
Publication host provisioning works with Apache on Debian and Ubuntu.
The Docker image can now write AVIF, so `.avif` alternative versions of images work out of the box.
Interlaced videos are now deinterlaced when their web versions are built.
The audio encoder for video and audio derivatives is chosen from what the configured ffmpeg can actually encode, and a failed encode names its error.
The profile permissions tree opens in a fraction of a second instead of several seconds.
Published files survive a power cut, and deleting a record no longer races a running publication into the same directory.
Resetting a hierarchy to its seed can no longer delete it without restoring it.
Local ontology overrides now apply to the node they point at, and change only what they state.
The Publication server API maintenance panel shows its "Open Swagger UI" buttons again.
Creating a site twice at the same moment can no longer overwrite or delete the first site.
Deleting a site while an agent session or a build is running is refused, and no longer blocks the site name.
Site builder state survives a power cut, and a damaged driver record is reported at startup.
A second Site Builder started by hand no longer stops the running service's agent runs.
Administrators' toolbars now show only the tools their profile grants.
Rebuilding a user's activity statistics can no longer lose them half-way.
A database backup counts only once it has been read back completely.
A database backup that is still being written no longer appears as a backup.
A publication run that crashes, is cancelled or meets another run now publishes exactly what it should — and large archives no longer exhaust memory.
Duplicating a record now files the history of a transliterable or IRI field in the language it was saved in.
Regenerating the media cache no longer undoes an upload made while it runs.
A move_* data transform can be stopped, and only one runs at a time.
A failed ontology update now says why, inside the Update ontology panel
The Update ontology panel scrolls to its result
Updating the ontology works from every configured master, not only the first
A site builder turn whose egress gate fails to close now still ends, instead of leaving the session running forever.
A data update now applies completely or not at all, and two updates can no longer run at once.
Error reports now include logged client errors
An update server with no public host now says so, instead of sending download links that point at localhost.
Time machine restore no longer fails on installs whose outbound host allowlist is empty.
The multi-instance Apache example now sets an empty `DocumentRoot` and the entry redirects.
The developer information bar is shown to developers and root again, on any server.
The RDF import no longer shows the internal address a refused link resolved to.
Related-record lists answer one bounded page, and say so when they cut it.
The test suite now runs its diffusion gates against its own MariaDB server, never an installation's.
Each release is published as a signed multi-architecture image, with the same digest on every Dédalo registry.
Tool authors can read other sites through `harvestFetch`, a harvesting door that obeys robots.txt and paces its requests.
The developer install and its test suite work over a PostgreSQL socket, never prompt for a password, and keep the dev server on this machine.
A save whose value is not shaped like the field's data is now refused instead of stored.
The client-library version table in the manual is generated from the pins, so it can no longer go stale.
A refused save no longer leaves an empty record behind.
A relation search with an unreadable value now fails with an error instead of quietly matching every record.
